what_happened: The agent ran a hand-written push loop to sync Athena's local branch with GitHub during a running batch. The sync hit a CHANGELOG conflict. The loop did not stop and kept retrying, so Athena's shared working copy sat mid-merge for about a minute. The agent aborted the merge, then recorded GitHub's old copies of the commits as merged without changing any files. No job work was judged bad.
cause: Athena lets the person running Athena commands write into the working tree that drain and landing use, and nothing tells the command that a landing is in progress or blocks it. Athena has no tracked command that syncs local history with GitHub after a landing rewrites the branch. The person falls back on a hand-written loop with no stop on conflict, so safe use depends on their own care. This is the same cause as the other hand-command mistakes: the person acts on shared state without Athena showing or guarding its current state.
prevention: Add a code check in a tracked Athena push/sync command. It refuses to run while a drain or landing holds the working copy. It runs the sync in a separate clone or worktree, not the shared tree. It stops at the first conflict and leaves the tree clean. It reconciles GitHub's old copies of rewritten commits explicitly, by recording them as merged with no file changes, instead of by a merge retry loop.
proposed_request: Add an `athena sync` command that pushes the local branch to GitHub and reconciles GitHub's older copies of commits that landing rewrote. Outcome: the command never leaves Athena's shared working copy mid-merge or dirty. It refuses to run while a drain or landing is in progress and says why. It does its merge work in a separate worktree. It stops on the first conflict (for example in CHANGELOG.md), aborts cleanly, and reports the conflicting file. When GitHub holds old copies of commits that landing rewrote, it records them as merged without changing any files. Acceptance: a test with a fixture built from a real landing rewrite shows a clean tree after a conflict; a test shows the command refuses while a landing is marked in progress; a test shows the old-copy case ends with no file changes and a recorded merge.
